A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Random Min study on quasar-convex optimisation. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F support comparison, including the new Appendix E.7 in v3. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original RM-versus-GD experiments on dynamical systems, SVMs, generalised linear models, reinforcement learning, RNNs and synthetic objectives.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds CMA-ES comparisons and a nonlinear black-box system-identification experiment in Section 4.2 and Appendix E.7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects sampling and averaging indices from 0,...,t to 1,...,t and replaces h with h_k in the projected update. These are limited pseudocode corrections aligning it with the existing description; Gaussian estimation, projection, minibatching and Armijo variants were already present.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix E.7 add a nonlinear black-box identification scenario: the existing five-mass mechanical chain gains actuator saturation and Coulomb friction, with gradients unavailable to the optimiser. This extends system-identification coverage while retaining all earlier tasks and datasets.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates GD and its projected or Armijo variants as comparators. v3 adds CMA-ES to the mechanical-system comparison in Figure 3 and evaluates it in the new nonlinear experiment in Figure 5. Existing GD comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new nonlinear experiment introduces 200 length-300 sequences, quarter-sequence burn-in, specified initial perturbations and 300 RM iterations with h=0.01 and smoothing 0.0001. New CMA-ES comparisons use population 18 and initial scale 0.05. Retained experiments have no identified substantive setting revisions; their newly disclosed settings belong under D1.

E4.justification: The nonlinear case study adds evidence comparing fixed-step RM with Armijo RM, examining how step-size selection affects convergence under black-box nonlinear dynamics. The existing smoothing-parameter and batch-size sensitivity experiment in Appendix E.6 is retained; its expanded explanation does not constitute a new ablation.

E5.justification: New Figure 3 explicitly reports five-run averaging and shaded variability for the mechanical-system comparison, supplementing the retained unbanded Figure 2. Figure 5 reports three-run averages with variability for the new nonlinear experiment. These additions do not establish increased run counts for retained results.

E6.justification: New Figures 3 and 5 report additional loss-versus-CPU-time outcomes, showing lower late-time loss for Armijo RM than CMA-ES in the illustrated comparisons. Tables 1–2 retain their numerical values, and existing performance plots are retained. These are additional results, rather than improved scores replacing earlier results.

T1.justification: Definition 2 introduces an admissible parameter set A; Theorems 3–4 require h in A, and Theorem 4 explicitly requires strong proximal quasar-convexity. Corollary 1 changes its iteration-bound coefficient from 4 to 8; Corollary 4 changes 16 to 64 in its batch bound and 4aε to 2aε in its smoothing bound. Theorem 2 excludes the step-size endpoint, and Remarks 3–4 add rate comparisons. The principal bounds and appendix proofs otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contribution statements retain the same convergence-rate claims, introduction of proximal quasar-convexity, variance-reduction guarantee and empirical competitiveness claim. Added experiments and refined formal conditions do not redefine those central contributions.

C2.justification: New Remarks 3–4 discuss differences from first-order complexity bounds in terms of step sizes and available information. Section 4.2 explains applicability when only nonlinear simulator outputs are accessible, and Section 5 identifies Armijo convergence analysis as future work. Appendix F's smoothing-based mechanism explanation is essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies t=1 across several retained experiments, gives the GLM smoothing parameter, explains function-versus-gradient call counts and discloses the Armijo maximum step size. It also supplies CMA-ES parameters and detailed nonlinear simulator and data-generation instructions in Appendix E.7. These disclosures do not demonstrate changes to the earlier implementations.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hansen's CMA-ES tutorial and Wang et al. (2020) on zeroth-order minimax optimisation. It expands motivation connecting quasar-convex applications with unavailable gradients and explicitly compares rates with already-cited Jin and Hinder results. The claimed novelty and overall research positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v3 adds a motivation paragraph and local explanations, repairs the fragmented opening of Section 4, and inserts Section 4.2 and Appendix E.7 without broadly reorganising the paper. Author affiliations and acknowledgments are updated. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds two CPU-time comparison plots as Figures 3 and 5 and redraws the recurrent-network diagram, formerly Figure 11 and now Figure 13. Existing performance figures are retained and renumbered or repositioned; table structures remain unchanged. The overall visual format is preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects concrete theorem conditions and finite-accuracy constants, fills implementation gaps, and addresses v2's reliance on GD comparisons by adding CMA-ES evidence. These improve precision, reproducibility and empirical relevance. The gains remain limited: the new nonlinear simulator is not shown to satisfy the smooth quasar-convex assumptions, and Remark 3's new alternative-step-size claim lacks a supporting derivation consistent with the retained proof.
